simple: All the steps that turn your source files into a program you can run.
analogy: Translating every recipe card and binding them into one cookbook.
precise: The sequence preprocess, compile, assemble, link; g++ runs all four when you give it .cpp files and -o name.
source: D3 of F2-01, R1 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The first step: it handles the lines that start with #, such as #include.
analogy: A copy clerk who pastes shared pages into a recipe card before it goes to the translator.
precise: The phase of translation that executes directives such as #include (which inserts the text of a header) and produces one long text; g++ -E stops after it.
source: D2 of F2-01, D3 of F2-01, R1 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One .cpp file together with everything it includes.
analogy: One recipe card after the clerk has pasted in all the shared pages.
precise: A source file plus all headers and source files included through #include, minus lines skipped by conditional directives; each one is compiled separately.
source: D2 of F2-01, D1 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The processor's instructions written as short words you can read.
analogy: The recipe in the head chef's own kitchen language, still on paper.
precise: A text form of machine instructions (here x86-64, in the AT&T style that GCC writes); g++ -S stops after producing it.
source: D3 of F2-01, D5 of F2-01, R1 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The machine-code version of one source file. It is not a program yet.
analogy: A translated card with blank spaces where page numbers of other cards must go.
precise: The output of compiling and assembling one translation unit (g++ -c, a .o file; on this machine an "ELF 64-bit LSB relocatable" file) holding machine code, a symbol table and notes for the linker.
source: D3 of F2-01, D4 of F2-01, R1 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A name that an object file offers to others, or asks others for.
analogy: A page title ("Price list") or a note "see the price list".
precise: An entry in an object file's symbol table that names a function or variable; nm marks a symbol defined in the code section with T and an undefined one with U.
source: D4 of F2-01, D6 of F2-01, R1 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The program that joins object files into one program and connects each use of a name to its definition.
analogy: The kitchen manager who binds the cards and writes in every page number.
precise: A tool (here ld, started by g++ through collect2) that combines object files and libraries, resolves every undefined symbol to exactly one definition, and writes an executable.
source: D4 of F2-01, D5 of F2-01, R2 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The linker's message when code uses a name but no object file defines it.
analogy: "I was told to look up the price list, but nobody gave me one."
precise: A link error reported by ld as undefined reference to `name', listing the function and object file that used the name.
source: R2 of F2-01, D4 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The way C++ writes a function's parameter types into its symbol name.
analogy: Writing "price list (by dish number)" as the page title, not only "price list".
precise: The encoding of a C++ name and its parameter types into one symbol, for example _Z10dish_pricei for dish_price(int) in this build; nm -C turns it back into readable form.
source: R1 of F2-01, D7 of F2-01, D6 of F2-01 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The actual thing stored, such as 7, 2.9, 'A' or true.
analogy: What is inside the container.
precise: The meaning of the bits of an object, interpreted according to the object's type.
source: D2 of F2-02, D1 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: An operator that tells you how many bytes a type uses.
analogy: Reading the container's capacity printed on its side.
precise: sizeof(T) gives the number of bytes of an object of type T as a std::size_t; sizeof(char) is 1 by definition.
source: D2 of F2-02, R1 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A whole-number type with no minus sign, used for sizes and counts.
analogy: A counter that can only count up from zero.
precise: The unsigned integer type of the result of sizeof, declared in <cstddef>; 8 bytes in this build.
source: D2 of F2-02, R1 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Turning a value of one type into a value of another type.
analogy: Pouring from one container into another shape.
precise: Producing a value of a target type from a value of a source type; implicit when the compiler does it by itself (for example int to double in 7.0 / 2), explicit when you ask for it.
source: D2 of F2-02, R2 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The way to say "convert this, I mean it".
analogy: Pouring on purpose, with your name on the label.
precise: An explicit conversion expression, static_cast<T>(e), for conversions the language defines, such as double to int (which drops the fraction).
source: D1 of F2-02, R2 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A conversion that can lose part of the value.
analogy: Pouring 2.9 litres into a rack of whole bottles.
precise: A conversion such as double to int, or to a type that cannot represent the value; forbidden inside brace initialization { }, where g++ reports "narrowing conversion".
source: D2 of F2-02, R4 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Cutting off the fraction instead of rounding.
analogy: Throwing away whatever does not fill a whole bottle.
precise: The double-to-integer conversion discards the fractional part, moving towards zero: 2.9 becomes 2 and −2.9 becomes −2 in this build.
source: D2 of F2-02, R2 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A calculation with int whose true answer is too big (or too small) for int.
analogy: Pouring more into a jug than it can hold.
precise: An arithmetic result of a signed integer type that is outside its range; it is undefined behaviour, and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reported it in this build.
source: D2 of F2-02, R6 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Something the C++ rules do not allow, where the program may then do anything.
analogy: A recipe step the kitchen rules forbid; nobody promises what happens if a cook does it anyway.
precise: Behaviour for which the standard imposes no requirements; the program may seem to work, give wrong answers or crash.
source: D2 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Going below zero (or above the top) on an unsigned type jumps to the other end.
analogy: A counter with no minus sign that rolls round.
precise: Unsigned arithmetic is done modulo 2n for an n-bit type, so 12 − 14 gives 264 − 2 = 18,446,744,073,709,551,614 for the 64-bit std::size_t of this build.
source: D2 of F2-02, R7 of F2-02 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The order in which a program's statements run.
analogy: The rules card at the pass that says which step comes next.
precise: The sequence of executed statements, changed by selection statements (if, switch), iteration statements (for, while, do) and jump statements (break, continue, return).
source: D2 of F2-03, D1 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A list of tests where the first true one wins.
analogy: Reading the rules card from the top and following the first rule that fits.
precise: Nested if/else statements written as if (a) … else if (b) … else …; the conditions are tested in order and only the first true branch runs.
source: D1 of F2-03, R5 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A way to pick one of many actions by comparing one value with fixed choices.
analogy: Sorting order slips by the letter written on them.
precise: switch (expr) { case c1: … } jumps to the case label whose constant equals the value of the integer or character expression, or to default if none does.
source: D2 of F2-03, R1 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: When the program runs on into the next case because nothing stopped it.
analogy: A cook who finishes the soup and carries on making noodles too.
precise: Execution continuing past the end of one case's statements into the next label; with -Wextra g++ warns "this statement may fall through" (an error under -Werror).
source: R4 of F2-03, D3 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: "Stop this loop or this switch now."
analogy: "The kitchen closes": stop taking slips.
precise: A jump statement that ends the innermost enclosing loop or switch; inside a switch in a loop it leaves only the switch.
source: D2 of F2-03, R1 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: "Skip the rest of this round and start the next one."
analogy: Table 3 is closed tonight: skip it and set the next table.
precise: A jump statement that ends the current iteration of the innermost loop; in a for loop the increment still runs.
source: D2 of F2-03, R2 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A loop that runs its body first and checks the condition afterwards.
analogy: Taste the soup, then decide whether to taste again.
precise: do statement while (condition); executes the statement at least once, then repeats while the condition is true.
source: D2 of F2-03, R2 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: && and || stop as soon as the answer is known.
analogy: "If guests have arrived and each eats a lot" — if no guests arrived, you do not even think about how much they eat.
precise: The right operand of && is not evaluated if the left is false; the right operand of || is not evaluated if the left is true.
source: D2 of F2-03, R1 of F2-03 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The function gets its own copy of the argument.
analogy: A photocopy of the order slip.
precise: A parameter of a non-reference type is initialized as a copy of the argument; changes to it do not affect the caller (R1: the pot was unchanged after add_salt_to_copy).
source: D1 of F2-04, R1 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Another name for an existing variable.
analogy: Handing over the real pot instead of a copy.
precise: A reference (T&) is an alias bound to an object when it is initialized; every use of the reference uses that object.
source: D1 of F2-04, D2 of F2-04, R1 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The function works on the caller's own variable.
analogy: The sauce station adds salt straight into the real pot.
precise: A parameter of type T& binds to the argument, so changes through it change the caller's object; the argument must be a modifiable variable.
source: D1 of F2-04, R1 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A reference that may be read but not used to change anything.
analogy: "Taste the real pot, but do not add anything."
precise: A parameter of type const T&: no copy is made, and assigning through it is a compile error ("assignment of read-only reference").
source: D1 of F2-04, R3 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Several functions with the same name but different parameter lists.
analogy: Two stations with the same sign, chosen by what is written on the slip.
precise: Functions in the same scope with one name and different parameter types or counts; for each call the compiler selects the best match by the argument types (overload resolution).
source: D2 of F2-04, R2 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A value a parameter takes when the caller leaves it out.
analogy: "Unless told otherwise, 0.1 kg of rice per portion."
precise: An initializer written in a function declaration, such as double kilograms_per_portion = 0.1; the compiler inserts it at each call that omits the argument.
source: D2 of F2-04, R2 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The part of the program where a name can be used.
analogy: A station's own notepad: other stations cannot read it.
precise: The region of program text in which a declaration is visible; a parameter or local variable is visible from its declaration to the end of its block.
source: D2 of F2-04, D1 of F2-04 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: An object that holds many values of one type.
analogy: The spike of slips, the muffin tin, the line of handwriting.
precise: A standard-library class that stores a collection of elements and gives access to them, such as std::vector<T>, std::array<T, N> and (for characters) std::string.
source: D1 of F2-05, D2 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Add one element at the end of a vector.
analogy: Pushing one more slip onto the spike.
precise: The std::vector member function that appends a copy of its argument, increasing size() by one; pop_back() removes the last element.
source: D2 of F2-05, R1 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: How many elements a container holds right now.
analogy: Counting the slips on the spike.
precise: A member function returning the number of elements as an unsigned type (std::size_t-like); valid indexes are 0 to size() - 1.
source: D2 of F2-05, R1 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Get an element by index, but check the index first.
analogy: A cook who counts the slips before reaching for one.
precise: A member function that returns the element at an index and throws std::out_of_range if the index is not less than size(); operator[] does no such check.
source: D2 of F2-05, D1 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The special answer "not found" from find.
analogy: "There is no tea on this slip."
precise: A constant equal to the largest value of std::string::size_type, returned by search functions such as find when there is no match.
source: D2 of F2-05, R2 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Copy a piece of a string.
analogy: Copying only the words "table 7" from the slip.
precise: s.substr(pos, count) returns a new string with up to count characters starting at index pos; without count, everything to the end.
source: D2 of F2-05, R2 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Using an index that is not inside the container.
analogy: Reaching past the last slip into empty air.
precise: Accessing an element with an index ≥ size() (or negative) through []; undefined behaviour, detected in this build by AddressSanitizer as a "heap-buffer-overflow".
source: D2 of F2-05, R6 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A checker built into the program that stops it when it touches memory it should not.
analogy: A kitchen inspector who stops service the moment a cook reaches into the wrong shelf.
precise: A compiler instrumentation (-fsanitize=address) that adds checks around memory accesses and prints a report (kind of error, address, stack of calls, where the memory was allocated) before aborting.
source: D3 of F2-05, R6 of F2-05 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Your own type that groups several named values.
analogy: An order ticket with labelled boxes.
precise: A class type declared with the keyword struct, whose members are public by default; each object of the type contains one object of each data member.
source: D1 of F2-06, D2 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: One named value inside a struct.
analogy: One labelled box on the ticket.
precise: A data member declared inside the struct, accessed with the dot operator, as in order.table (or order.quantity through a reference).
source: D1 of F2-06, R1 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A starting value written next to a member.
analogy: A ticket printed with "Quantity: 1" already filled in.
precise: An initializer in a member declaration, such as int quantity = 1;, used whenever an object is created without another value for that member.
source: D2 of F2-06, R1 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Filling in a struct's members with a list in braces.
analogy: Writing the values into the ticket's boxes from left to right.
precise: Initialization of an aggregate (such as a simple struct) from a braced list; the values go to the members in declaration order, and members without a value get their default member initializer.
source: D2 of F2-06, R4 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Naming each member as you fill it in.
analogy: Writing "Table: 2" instead of just "2".
precise: A C++20 form of aggregate initialization, {.table = 2, .dish = "soup"}; the names must follow the declaration order, which g++ checks ("designator order … does not match declaration order").
source: D2 of F2-06, R3 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Unused bytes the compiler puts between or after members.
analogy: Empty space on the ticket so that each box starts on a printed grid line.
precise: Bytes inserted so that each member starts at an offset that is a multiple of its alignment, and so that the struct's size is a multiple of its own alignment; measured with sizeof and offsetof.
source: D3 of F2-06, R2 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The rule "this type must start at an address that is a multiple of N".
analogy: Boxes that may start only on certain grid lines.
precise: The required address multiple of a type, given by alignof; 8 for double in this build.
source: D2 of F2-06, R2 of F2-06 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A file of declarations that other files include.
analogy: The printed menu: names and prices, no recipes.
precise: A source file, usually ending in .h or .hpp, whose text is copied into each file that names it in an #include directive.
source: D1 of F2-07, D2 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: "Paste that file here."
analogy: Stapling a copy of the menu to your page.
precise: A preprocessor directive that replaces itself with the contents of the named file; "units.h" searches the including file's directory first, <string> searches the system directories.
source: D3 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The full version of a function, with its body.
analogy: The recipe itself.
precise: A declaration that also provides the entity: for a function, the declaration together with its body.
source: D2 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Many declarations are fine; a normal function may have only one definition in the whole program.
analogy: A dish may appear on many menus, but it has exactly one recipe.
precise: Every non-inline function used in the program must be defined exactly once across all translation units; inline functions may be defined in each unit that uses them, identically.
source: D2 of F2-07, R5 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: Three lines that make a header count only once per file.
analogy: A stamp "menu already attached" so you do not staple it twice.
precise: #ifndef NAME / #define NAME … #endif around a header's contents, so that a second inclusion into the same translation unit produces nothing.
source: D3 of F2-07, R4 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: The linker found the same function body twice.
analogy: Two different recipes for the same dish.
precise: A linker error reported when two object files both define the same non-inline symbol.
source: R5 of F2-07, D4 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A word that allows the same function body in several files.
analogy: A tiny recipe printed on every menu, the same everywhere.
precise: A function specifier that permits a definition in every translation unit that uses it; the linker keeps one copy.
source: D2 of F2-07, R6 of F2-07 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A line that says "this must be true here", and stops the program if it is not.
analogy: The head chef's check at the pass.
precise: The macro assert(expression) from <cassert>; if the expression is false, it prints the file, line, function and expression, then calls std::abort.
source: D1 of F2-08, R3 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A check that the compiler does, before the program exists.
analogy: Checking the recipe card before anyone starts cooking.
precise: A declaration static_assert(constant-expression, "message");; if the expression is false, compilation fails with the message.
source: D2 of F2-08, R2 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A small check of one function, with an input and the answer you expect.
analogy: Tasting one sauce on its own.
precise: Code that calls a unit (here: one function) with chosen inputs and compares the results with expected values computed independently.
source: D3 of F2-08, R1 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A second program whose only job is to run the tests.
analogy: A tasting session before opening.
precise: An executable built from the code under test plus a test file with its own main; exit code 0 means all tests passed.
source: R1 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: What must be true before a function may be called.
analogy: "Only plates with a ticket go on the pass."
precise: A condition on the arguments or state at entry; checking it with assert documents it and catches wrong callers during testing.
source: D3 of F2-08, D4 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: An input at the border: zero, empty, the smallest or largest value.
analogy: An order for zero guests.
precise: A test input at the boundary of a function's valid range or of a branch condition, where off-by-one and missing-case errors show up.
source: D3 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: A switch that turns every assert into nothing.
analogy: "Skip the checks tonight."
precise: A macro name; when it is defined (for example with -DNDEBUG) before <cassert> is included, assert(e) expands to nothing and e is not evaluated.
source: D1 of F2-08, R4 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)

simple: How close two decimal numbers must be to count as equal.
analogy: "Hot enough" is a range, not one exact degree.
precise: A bound eps such that |got - expected| < eps is accepted; needed because double results carry rounding (F2-02).
source: D5 of F2-08 (R = lab run in this build; D = book or manual cited by title only, pending verification at dossier gate G1)
